02-twin-actors:
Twin-core is re-lighting the world at dawn; your actors must look right in low key light. Priorities:
- ROVER: use the real CAD model (assets/models/rover_cad.glb) with correct PBR materials (brushed aluminium extrusion, black rubber rollers, PCB green, cable runs), mecanum wheels and rollers that really turn with the motion, suspension bob, headlights with visible beams in the mist, status LED, wheel spray and ruts decal, antenna flex.
- THE MOMENT: Wi-Fi sensing must be the most beautiful thing in the product: the transmitter's wavefronts sweep out, pass through the wall as it turns to glass, scatter off the hidden body, and return to the receiver as a bright thread; the disturbed subcarriers ripple; the body resolves from noise into a warm volumetric figure as the probability rises, then locks with one quiet pulse. Uncertainty is visible (a soft ellipsoid that tightens). Never a cartoon orange circle with a question mark: replace the current 'possible' marker with a thin, elegant uncertainty ellipse on the ground plus a faint flickering volume.
- DRONE: detailed body, spinning props with motion blur discs, gimbal, downward lidar curtain drawing a dense point cloud that stays and settles (colour by height, fading into the mesh), not scattered dots.
- TEAM: skinned or well-posed articulated rescuers with helmets, headlamps, jackets, walking cycles that plant their feet.
- ROUTE: a ribbon that draws itself on the ground with soft edges, flows around hazards (which push it visibly), and lights the way as the team walks. HAZARDS: physical (cracks, drip, gas shimmer, sliding mud) with a thin hatch, not flat red polygons.
60 fps; everything stops with reduced motion.

THE HERO: A HALL OF 900 PEOPLE WHO NEVER EXISTED.
The training set is real data you have: ~/Developer/rover-design-study/ml/data/people.json (900 people: posture standing or lying, height 1.20 to 1.95 m, shoulder, chest depth, yaw, zone, and 24 surface points with normals and areas per person) and the windows made from them (synth.npz, split by person). Show exactly those 900, each with their own height, build, posture and yaw, as life-size figures standing or lying in a vast, dark, wet-floored concrete hall, ranks receding into haze. Each figure is sculpted light-grey plaster, not a capsule: build one good human body in code (proper proportions, head, neck, shoulders, waist, hips, knees, feet, hands, clothing folds by displacement and normal detail; about 6 posture variants; three levels of detail; instanced) or bake one with Blender (/opt/homebrew/bin/blender, your own new script in tools/blender/, marching/remesh/subdivision sculpt, baked normal map) and morph it per person from their real numbers. Contact shadows, soft reflections in the wet floor, one huge soft overhead key and hard rim from behind, volumetric haze. Faces stay abstract: no eyes, no portraits.
Between them and the far wall: the network, a tall, thin, luminous instrument (monochrome, precise, the only other light), made of the real layers and real weights; every thread's opacity is a true weight, every particle a true activation.
THE STORY, one continuous eased camera move of about 26 s that loops with a held ending:
  1. Dark. One figure up close; it breathes / steps; a thin ripple of Wi-Fi passes through it, comes out changed, and the changed pattern (its real 52-channel window, as a fine ribbon of light) lifts off and flies to the network, which answers. Wrong. It stays dark.
  2. The camera rises: hundreds of ribbons lift off like a murmuration, streaming into the network; the threads, pure noise at first, visibly organise.
  3. With every training step the whole crowd is re-judged by the real model at that step (your recorded real run: about 40 checkpoints, per-person right / wrong on their own windows, test people marked by standing on a slightly raised platform, never trained on): each person the network finds warms from within, ember to glow; each it misses stays cold plaster. At first it flickers at random. By the end most moving people glow and most still ones are dark, because that is the truth (held-out, in simulation: 86.9 % of moving people found, 21.4 % of still ones). Split the hall so this reads at a glance: walking on one side of the aisle, still on the other. The unlit side IS the honest limit, and it is beautiful and a little haunting. Hold there.
The crowd is the chart. No other chart. Restraint: near-black, plaster grey, one warm colour (the person token) for found, cool white for radio. Think Antony Gormley's fields, Villeneuve's lighting, a Rockstar cutscene, not a tech demo. 60 fps at 1680x1000 (instancing, LOD, baked light, half-resolution haze and reflection, adaptive pixel ratio).
WORDS: headline (serif, lower left like every chapter): "Trained on people who never existed". One line: "900 simulated people taught it what a living body does to Wi-Fi." Two figures: training step, and moving people found (held out, in simulation), from the recorded run. At the end the line changes to: "It finds people who move.
